drhp.business: MLDL is a real estate development company in India that, through its subsidiaries and joint ventures, develops residential projects and industrial developments comprising integrated cities and industrial clusters (IC&IC). The residential portfolio is oriented towards premium/mid-premium housing with a gradual reduction in affordable-segment exposure, and is delivered through a mix of outright land acquisition, joint developments and society redevelopment. The IC&IC business operates plug-and-play industrial ecosystems with integrated infrastructure serving domestic and global enterprises …

risks.note: Management states the real estate industry is cyclical in nature and any downturn can impact the Company's performance; presence in both residential and industrial segments plus a premium/mid-premium focus is cited as the key mitigant, with the premium segment described as relatively more resilient than luxury.
risks.risk: Cyclicality of the real estate industry

risks.note: Inflation in commodity costs can impact profitability. Geopolitical events can influence energy prices and the cost of steel, cement, aluminium, glass and tiles, and supply disruptions particularly in aluminium and tiles may lead to cost pressures; mitigated through cost-escalation provisions, value engineering, long-term/forward contracts and price revisions.
risks.risk: Commodity cost inflation and geopolitical disruption of construction inputs

risks.note: Listed as a key operational risk; residential revenue depends on absorption of launched and sustenance inventory, and market volatility can influence homebuyer sentiment given the high-value nature of residential purchases.
risks.risk: Sales risk - inability to sell projects as per plan

risks.note: Inability to complete and deliver projects within timelines is flagged as a key operational risk, alongside difficulties in appointment and retention of contractors and manpower; addressed through a structured control framework with assigned ownership.
risks.risk: Execution and delivery risk leading to cost overruns

risks.note: Inability to attract and retain talent is an explicit operational risk; permanent-employee turnover disclosed in the BRSR at 20.85% (IC&IC) and 18.79% (Residential) for FY 2025-26, with IC&IC turnover higher than the prior year.

Flagged as an operational risk that can lead to penalties and litigation; managed through corporate governance policies, a Code of Conduct for all associates, an ethics helpline and whistle-blower mechanism routed to the Business Ethics & Governance Committee or the Audit Committee Chairperson.
risks.risk: Fraud, unethical practices and non-compliance with laws and regulations

risks.note: Management explicitly cites increased exposure to security breaches and exploitation of vulnerabilities driven by rapid advancements in AI as an operational risk.

The sector remains sensitive to changes in government policy; procedural delays in approvals related to land acquisition and development are described as a structural challenge and unfavourable regulatory changes may impact business performance; mitigated by disciplined land acquisition with thorough due diligence.
risks.risk: Policy and regulatory risk, including approval delays for land acquisition and development
